conventional.policy_description: Country-by-country GILTI at 21% and no QBAI exemption. Published estimate: raises about \$374B over ten years (Treasury, FY2025 Green Book).

credibility.no_band_reason: the one pre-registered corporate row is a statutory rate change, not a GILTI, FDII or Pillar Two reform
credibility.own_row_caption: Unfitted reconstruction, 38.4% from -$374B (U.S. Treasury) — no constant is fitted to this figure.
limitations: holdout labels follow the locked post-2026-05-02 regression protocol; they are not retroactive historical out-of-sample claims.
No pre-registered out-of-sample row scores a policy of this class, so this model's accuracy on one has not been measured.

GILTI is modelled as an aggregate rate change on a single CFC income pool; the country-by-country mechanics that drive the Treasury proposal (per-jurisdiction blending, loss ring-fencing, the foreign tax credit haircut) are not represented. The jurisdictional distribution added for the base-overlap term is used for the overlap share only, not to set this level.

Two of the constants behind this row describe themselves as fitted: gilti_cbc_revenue_multiplier 1.20 ('Treasury calibrated') and gilti_ftc_offset_rate 0.40 ('Calibration factor'). Treasury OTA prices the whole CFC active-income preference at $383,830M over FY2025-2034 against the module's implied $271B, which is the identity that would replace both.

The row's proposal text matches this factory's shape (jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction, rate to 21%, QBAI eliminated) but its scope also covers the inversion and related-reform provisions the module does not implement, so the residual is an upper bound on the module's own miss. The two fitted constants above were set against the superseded figure and were deliberately not retuned.
credibility.caption: No out-of-sample band: the one pre-registered corporate row is a statutory rate change, not a GILTI, FDII or Pillar Two reform. The 44 pre-registered Tier 1 rows are the only tier that measures this model's accuracy, and none of them scores a policy of this kind.
